items.detail: Root cause: the module-level `kept` array was only emptied by PrebuiltPage's ref, i.e. only if the routes' Suspense fallback mounted. If the route code landed between main.tsx's 8 s start and React's first render (lazyRoute rendered the page directly), or the first render failed to the error panel, `kept` survived and the next suspending navigation showed the old pre-built page under the live header. Fix: new `dropPrebuiltPage()` in src/lib/prebuiltPage.ts, called from `useLayoutEffect(dropPrebuiltPage, [])` in App itself (src/App.tsx). I put it in App, outside ChunkErrorBoundary, not in AppShell next to clearFallbackMark: a layout effect in AppShell never runs when the first render throws to the panel, and App's runs after the first commit whatever that commit rendered. Children commit first, so the fallback's ref still takes the page when it does mount. The existing 'stays on screen' test now runs with the drop in place, which proves that ordering. App's JSX was re-indented into a block body. No pixel/tracking code touched.

items.issue: 3. Wishlist handles in the main chunk (src/components/WishlistDrawer.tsx)
items.detail: Root cause: WishlistDrawer is imported eagerly by App.tsx and statically imported JEWELLERY_HANDLES to choose each link. Fix: WishlistItem gets an optional kind ('jewellery' | 'apparel'), set where each item is saved: JewelCard, JewelDetail and JewelDetailNext save 'jewellery'. ProductGallery saves 'apparel' (it only renders on the outfit page; ProductDetail redirects jewellery first). ProductCard uses isJewelleryProduct(shopifyProduct), because 'You May Also Like' draws from the whole store. The drawer links from kind. For items saved before this change (no kind), it dynamic-imports @/data/jewelleryHandles only when it opens holding such an item, so links match the previous build: /jewellery/<h> for jewellery, /product/<h> otherwise. Which fallback is correct: /product/<id> alone does reach the right page, because ProductDetail's first-render hop covers JEWELLERY_HANDLES plus the bundled pieces and a Shopify lookup covers the rest. But it changes the href, downloads the ProductDetail chunk, and PixelEvents fires an extra PageView for the /product/ hop, so it is only the stand-in while the lookup is in flight or if it fails. jewelleryHandles was added to optionalChunk.ts, so a failed lookup never reloads the page. Pixel calls and values are unchanged; toggleItem's AddToWishlist payload is the same fields. npx vite build: the entry (index-*.js) no longer contains 'amethyst-carre-bracelet'. Baseline 63ed576: index-BAK7qpxN.js amethyst=1, 95,915 B gzip. Final: index-DyDNz_Ed.js amethyst=0, 94,931 B gzip. The list is now its own chunk, jewelleryHandles-Yy5OagZw.js. index.html still carries the handles in the pre-boot redirect map, by design. Browser run (served build, 360px, NO_REPORT aborted, webdriver=false, Shiprocket stubbed): the chunk was not requested on page load and was requested when the wishlist opened with a legacy item. The 4 saved items linked to /jewellery/prism-riviere-bracelet, /product/blush-of-dawn, /jewellery/amethyst-carre-bracelet (legacy) and /product/ivory-whisper-co-ord-set (legacy). No page errors.

items.detail: This is a real regression from this branch (6c04e30 added keepPrebuiltPage; base has no prebuiltPage.ts). The root cause: the stand-in check relied only on <html data-nf-fallback>, and the guard removes that mark itself after 10 s, so a slow app start found it already gone. The fix adds isStandInPage() in src/lib/fallbackGuard.ts. It returns true if the mark is set, or if the guard's own inline script is in the document on any address other than the homepage. Only dist/index.html carries that script (prerender writes it into the shell alone), and scripts stay in the DOM, so the check never expires. The homepage addresses are now one HOME_PATHS list shared with the guard script, and the generated guard output is byte-for-byte unchanged (compared before and after with tsx). keepPrebuiltPage() now calls isStandInPage(). No index.html, pixel or checkout code was touched, and nothing needs re-publishing beyond the normal build.
items.test: src/lib/prebuiltPage.test.tsx: 'never keeps the homepage standing in for another address after the guard's mark is gone'. It puts the real withFallbackGuard head in via innerHTML, so the script does not run and the mark stays absent, and sets the path to /jewellery/star-point-band. It failed before the fix (the homepage h1 was kept) and passes after. 'keeps the homepage on its own address, guard and all' covers / and /index.html. src/lib/fallbackGuard.test.ts adds isStandInPage tests: it agrees with the guard script's own decision for 7 addresses after the mark is gone, it is true while the mark is on, and it is false for a page's own file.
